features.name: Landing_Page
features.purpose: Introduces BWS4, explains that it and every example app were built with Spec4, and lists the available example apps so visitors can choose one to explore.

invocation.trigger: A visitor opens the site's home address or chooses the home entry in site navigation.

inputs.name: Example app roster
inputs.description: Name, one-line summary and destination of each example app (RAG, Embeddings, Single Call, Chained Calls, Planning Agent, Orchestrated Subagents, Multi-Agent Collaboration, ReAct Loop, Router, Tool Use).

outputs.primary: A page that explains BWS4 and the Spec4 origin and lists every example app with a way to open each.
outputs.format: Web page with introductory text and a list of app entries
outputs.schema_notes: Each entry shows the app's label and a short description. Labels match site navigation exactly, including 'ReAct Loop' and 'Router'.

success_criteria: The page states that BWS4 and all example apps were built with Spec4.
Every available example app appears exactly once and opens the correct app.
The page is usable immediately on first visit with no noticeable warm-up delay.

failure_modes.mode: An app is added or renamed but the list is not updated
failure_modes.mitigation: Draw the list and the site navigation from a single roster so they cannot disagree.

failure_modes.mode: A listed entry leads to a missing page
failure_modes.mitigation: Check that every roster entry resolves to a working page before release.

features.name: RAG_Example_App
features.purpose: Illustrates retrieval-augmented generation: the visitor asks a question, relevant passages are retrieved from a small public space-exploration dataset, and an answer is generated from them. It is educational rather than practically useful.

invocation.trigger: The visitor submits a question in the RAG example app.

inputs.name: Question
inputs.description: A question the visitor wants answered from the dataset.

inputs.name: Dataset documents
inputs.description: The small public dataset, already embedded and indexed.

outputs.primary: A generated answer together with the retrieved passages it was based on.
outputs.format: Answer text plus a list of source passages with their titles
outputs.schema_notes: The retrieval step and the generation step are shown separately so the pattern is visible.

success_criteria: Retrieved passages are relevant to the question and shown to the visitor.
The answer is grounded in the retrieved passages.
A short educational overview explains the RAG pattern.
The page uses the common example-app layout.

failure_modes.mode: Retrieval returns weakly related passages
failure_modes.mitigation: Show the passages so the visitor can see the cause, and have the answer say when the passages do not cover the question.

failure_modes.mode: Question is outside the dataset's subject
failure_modes.mitigation: State that the dataset does not cover it instead of inventing an answer.

failure_modes.mode: Generation unavailable or usage cap reached
failure_modes.mitigation: Show a clear message and keep the retrieved passages visible.

features.name: Shared_Framework_Services
features.purpose: Provides the common capabilities every example app relies on: text generation through free hosted models, a small local embedding model with a 2D projection, web search, relational and vector data access, moderation, and shared usage caps. Gives all apps one consistent, always-warm foundation.

invocation.trigger: The service starts up, and afterwards any example app requests generation, embedding, search, retrieval, moderation or usage accounting.

inputs.name: Generation credential
inputs.description: Required in every environment (production, local development, tests). There is no placeholder value and no opt-out.

inputs.name: Moderation credential
inputs.description: Required in every environment for the moderation service, with the same strictness.

inputs.name: Service requests
inputs.description: Prompts, texts to embed, search queries and retrieval queries from the example apps.

inputs.name: Route descriptions source
inputs.description: Data used at startup to prepare the Router's route descriptions.

outputs.primary: Generated text, embedding vectors and 2D coordinates, search results, retrieved passages, moderation verdicts and remaining-usage information.
outputs.format: Structured responses consumed by the example apps
outputs.schema_notes: The embedding model and 2D projection are prepared once at startup and stay ready for the life of the process. Route-description preparation is best-effort. Hourly and daily usage caps are shared across all apps.

success_criteria: The service refuses to start if either required credential is missing, with a clear message.
With both credentials present, the service starts and embedding and projection are ready before the first visitor request.
A failure while preparing route descriptions is logged and the service still starts.
Shared usage caps are enforced consistently across all apps.

failure_modes.mode: A required credential is missing or invalid in some environment
failure_modes.mitigation: Fail at startup with a message naming the missing credential; never substitute a placeholder.

failure_modes.mode: The hosted free models are rate-limited or unavailable
failure_modes.mitigation: Return a clear, distinguishable 'service busy' outcome and keep prior results visible in the apps.

failure_modes.mode: Route-description preparation fails at startup
failure_modes.mitigation: Log the failure, start anyway, and let the Router report itself temporarily unavailable until preparation succeeds.

failure_modes.mode: The data store is unreachable
failure_modes.mitigation: Report a clear failure to the affected app and leave unaffected apps working.

features.name: Tool_Use_Integration
features.purpose: Lets example apps that need outside facts call the shared web search tool and receive result snippets, demonstrating tool use in agentic apps.

invocation.trigger: An example app decides to look something up and sends a search query.

inputs.name: Search query
inputs.description: The query written by a model or app.

inputs.name: Result limit
inputs.description: How many result snippets to return.

outputs.primary: A list of result snippets with titles and source addresses.
outputs.schema_notes: Each item has a title, a source address and a short text snippet. An empty list is a valid outcome.

success_criteria: A valid query returns relevant snippets promptly.
Each search is counted against the shared usage limits.
Failures are reported to the calling app as a distinct outcome, not as an empty result.

failure_modes.mode: Search service is unavailable or rate-limited
failure_modes.mitigation: Return a clear failure so the app can explain it candidly to the visitor.

failure_modes.mode: Query returns nothing useful
failure_modes.mitigation: Return an empty result and let the calling app decide whether to try again or stop.

failure_modes.mode: Search usage exceeds the allowance
failure_modes.mitigation: Count every search against the shared limits and refuse new ones when the limit is reached.

features.name: Embeddings_Example_App
features.purpose: Illustrates text embeddings through a visual explorer. Curated words, phrases and sentences are plotted in 2D so semantic clusters can be seen, and visitors can add their own text to see where it lands.

invocation.trigger: The visitor opens the app (curated points are shown), or enters custom text and submits it.

inputs.name: Curated examples
inputs.description: Pre-configured word and short-phrase categories (e.g. animals, emotions, tech terms) plus full sentences.

inputs.name: Custom text
inputs.description: Optional text the visitor wants placed on the plot.

outputs.primary: A 2D plot of all points where similar meanings sit near each other and the visitor's own text stands out in a distinct color.
outputs.format: Visual scatter plot with labelled points and a color legend
outputs.schema_notes: Adding custom text recalculates the projection so the new point is merged with the curated points. The shared embedding model is reused and no new model is introduced.

success_criteria: Curated categories visibly form clusters.
Custom text appears in a distinct color within the same recalculated projection.
A short educational overview explains embeddings.
The app uses the common layout and is listed on the landing page and in site navigation.

failure_modes.mode: Custom text is empty, extremely long or inappropriate
failure_modes.mitigation: Reject it with a clear message and apply the shared moderation check.

failure_modes.mode: Recalculated projection shifts the curated points confusingly
failure_modes.mitigation: Keep point arrangement as stable as possible and explain that positions are relative.

failure_modes.mode: Embedding capability not yet ready
failure_modes.mitigation: Show a temporary-unavailable message instead of a broken plot.

features.name: Single_Call_Example_App
features.purpose: Illustrates the single-call pattern: one direct request to a model producing one direct response with no retrieval, tools or chaining. Visitors can compare plain and structured responses.

invocation.trigger: The visitor submits a free-form prompt or picks a preset prompt (e.g. summarize, classify, extract) and runs it.

inputs.name: Prompt
inputs.description: Free-form text or one of the preset prompts.

inputs.name: Mode
inputs.description: Simple (plain text in, plain text out) or Structured (a response that conforms to a requested shape).

outputs.primary: The model's response; in Structured mode, both the structured request payload and the structured response are shown.
outputs.format: Plain text, or a pair of structured displays for request and response
outputs.schema_notes: Exactly one model call per run.

success_criteria: Each run makes exactly one model call.
Structured mode shows both the request and a response that conforms to the requested shape.
Switching modes changes only how the request is made and how the output is shown.
A short overview explains the pattern and when it is appropriate.

failure_modes.mode: Structured response does not match the requested shape
failure_modes.mitigation: Show the raw response with a clear note that it did not conform, rather than hiding it.

failure_modes.mode: Generation unavailable or usage cap reached
failure_modes.mitigation: Show a clear message that distinguishes the cause.

failure_modes.mode: Empty or oversized prompt
failure_modes.mitigation: Validate the prompt and explain the limit.

features.name: Chained_Calls_Example_App
features.purpose: Illustrates chained model calls where the first call's output feeds the second. The demo is limited to exactly two calls to conserve quota, though the pattern allows any number.

invocation.trigger: The visitor submits an initial request.

inputs.name: Initial request
inputs.description: The visitor's starting request for the first call.

outputs.primary: The first call's intermediate output and the second call's final output, both displayed, with each agent's role stated beforehand.
outputs.format: Two labelled text sections plus role descriptions
outputs.schema_notes: If the second step fails, the first output stays visible and the run reports a 'critique_failed' status while still completing successfully, as before.

success_criteria: Exactly two model calls are made per run.
The second call demonstrably receives the first call's output.
The page states that the two-call limit is a quota choice and that the pattern supports any number of calls.
A short overview explains the pattern.

failure_modes.mode: The first call fails
failure_modes.mitigation: Stop before the second call and explain clearly.

failure_modes.mode: The second call fails
failure_modes.mitigation: Keep the intermediate output visible and report the 'critique_failed' status.

failure_modes.mode: Shared usage cap reached
failure_modes.mitigation: Refuse before starting and say why.

features.name: Planning_Agent_Example_App
features.purpose: Illustrates plan-first agents with a trip-day planner. A planner call decomposes the goal into steps, the visitor sees the plan first, and executor calls then carry it out and compose a one-day itinerary.

invocation.trigger: The visitor submits a city and interests (planning), then chooses the next-step action to run the displayed plan.

inputs.name: City
inputs.description: Destination for the one-day itinerary.

inputs.name: Interests
inputs.description: What the visitor likes to do or see.

inputs.name: Search results
inputs.description: Results returned by the shared web search for research steps.

outputs.primary: A displayed plan of discrete steps, each step's result shown as it completes, ending in a one-day itinerary.
outputs.format: Ordered list of steps with results, then itinerary text
outputs.schema_notes: About 1 planner call plus 2–3 executor calls per run. The plan is fixed and shown before any step runs.

success_criteria: The plan appears before any step runs, and nothing runs until the visitor chooses the next-step action.
Steps run in sequence with each result displayed on completion.
Per-run model-call limits and the small per-visit run limit are shown clearly.
The overview cross-references the ReAct Loop app as the interleaved counterpart.
Run-limit and shared-cap messages are distinguishable.

failure_modes.mode: Planner produces an unusable or oversized plan
failure_modes.mitigation: Enforce the fixed step limit and show a clear message if the plan cannot be used.

failure_modes.mode: A research step finds nothing
failure_modes.mitigation: Mark the step as inconclusive and let the synthesis step say what was missing.

failure_modes.mode: Visit run limit or shared cap reached
failure_modes.mitigation: Disable input and the next-step action with an explanatory message while prior results stay visible.

features.name: Orchestrated_Subagents_Example_App
features.purpose: Illustrates an orchestrator that picks two specialists from a roster of four (Technical, Financial, Historical, Practical), delegates in parallel and merges their answers.

invocation.trigger: The visitor chooses a preset or types a question, then chooses the next-step action to dispatch after seeing the delegation decision.

inputs.name: Question
inputs.description: A curated preset (covering different pairings) or the visitor's own question.

outputs.primary: The delegation decision (two chosen specialists, rationale, and a brief for each), two parallel specialist columns with live status, and one merged final answer.
outputs.format: Decision panel, two parallel columns, final answer text
outputs.schema_notes: Exactly 3 model calls per run (1 orchestrator + 2 specialists). 3 runs per visit. A 'runs remaining' indicator is shown.

success_criteria: Exactly two distinct specialists are chosen from the four, each with a brief shown before dispatch.
The two specialists run concurrently with visible per-specialist status.
The orchestrator merges both answers into one response.
When runs are exhausted, input and the next-step action are disabled with an explanation, and earlier results stay visible.
Messaging distinguishes the 3-run visit limit from the shared daily cap.

failure_modes.mode: Orchestrator picks fewer or more than two specialists, or an unknown one
failure_modes.mitigation: Validate the decision and report a clear failure instead of dispatching.

failure_modes.mode: One specialist fails
failure_modes.mitigation: Show that column as failed and have the merge state which perspective is missing.

failure_modes.mode: Run limit or shared cap reached
failure_modes.mitigation: Block new runs with a message naming which limit was hit.

features.name: Multi_Agent_Collaboration_Example_App
features.purpose: Illustrates peer agents negotiating across a staged trust boundary. A Buyer agent and two rival Seller agents with private constraints exchange bids over an in-process, A2A-shaped message flow.

invocation.trigger: The visitor selects a preset procurement scenario, sets priority weighting, and starts the negotiation.

inputs.name: Scenario
inputs.description: A preset procurement scenario tuned to produce non-comparable bids.

inputs.name: Priority weighting
inputs.description: The visitor's priorities such as speed over price, full quantity required, or longest warranty.

outputs.primary: Buyer track (request for quote, counter-offers, award with rationale), two parallel seller columns with live status, an end-of-run reveal of each party's private constraints, and an optional chronological message-log view.
outputs.format: Parallel columns, buyer track, reveal panel, optional message log
outputs.schema_notes: One negotiation round with exactly 6 model calls; the request for quote is composed without a model. Each agent publishes an inspectable Agent Card; exchanges use task, message and artifact objects. Sellers never see each other's messages, enforced in code. No free text input. Standard hourly limits plus shared caps apply.

success_criteria: Exactly 6 model calls occur in the order: two initial bids, one buyer review issuing two counters, two best-and-final bids, one award.
No message ever passes from one seller to the other, as visible in the message log.
Different priorities can produce a different winner for the same scenario.
The reveal shows why each seller held firm or conceded.

The overview states that the A2A data model and interaction pattern are used without network transport, what a real deployment would add, and that this staged trust boundary would be over-engineering in a real system.

failure_modes.mode: A seller produces a bid that violates its own private constraints
failure_modes.mitigation: Check bids against the constraints and show the correction or failure candidly.

failure_modes.mode: A seller or the buyer call fails mid-run
failure_modes.mitigation: End the run with a clear partial state and keep completed steps on screen.

failure_modes.mode: Hourly or shared cap reached
failure_modes.mitigation: Refuse before starting and name the limit hit.

features.name: ReAct_Loop_Example_App
features.purpose: Illustrates the ReAct reason–act–observe loop on multi-hop questions, shown as a live trace in deliberate contrast with the plan-first Planning Agent and the single-decision Tool Use example.

invocation.trigger: The visitor picks one of five curated multi-hop questions or types their own, then starts the run.

inputs.name: Question
inputs.description: One of five presets (stored as questions only, never answers) or a free-form question.

inputs.name: Search results
inputs.description: Snippets returned by the shared web search for each search action.

outputs.primary: A live trace of thought, action (exact search query or decision to answer) and observation per cycle, ending in a final answer card citing its observations or a budget-exhausted card showing the partial trace and unresolved items.
outputs.format: Chronological trace plus an ending card, with a live cycle counter and a runs-remaining indicator
outputs.schema_notes: Up to about 8 searches plus 1 final-answer call per run. 2 runs per visit. No plan is shown and the visitor approves nothing mid-run.

success_criteria: Each later search visibly builds on the earlier observation.
The cycle counter (e.g. 'search 3 of 8') advances during the run.
Every run ends in exactly one of a final answer card or a budget-exhausted card, never a disguised answer.
The overview explains the contrast with Tool Use and Planning Agent, and notes that a model may state a first hop from its own knowledge on some presets.
When runs are exhausted, input and start are disabled with an explanation, earlier results stay visible, and messaging distinguishes the 2-run visit limit from the shared usage cap.

failure_modes.mode: Model loops or repeats the same query
failure_modes.mitigation: The fixed cycle cap ends the run in the budget-exhausted state.

failure_modes.mode: Searches return nothing useful
failure_modes.mitigation: Let the model reason about the gap; if unresolved, end candidly as budget-exhausted.

failure_modes.mode: Preset question becomes stale or ill-formed over time
failure_modes.mitigation: Because only questions are stored, answers refresh each run; an occasional check confirms each question still parses.

failure_modes.mode: Run limit or shared cap reached
failure_modes.mitigation: Block new runs with a message naming which limit applies.

features.name: Self_Hosted_Deployment
features.purpose: Runs BWS4 as a single always-on instance reachable at a secure public address with a valid certificate, serving both the web client and the services, while data stays in the external relational and vector store. It removes the previous host and the cold-start delay.

invocation.trigger: The release is put live, and thereafter every visitor request to the public address.

inputs.name: Built web client
inputs.description: The finished visitor-facing application.

inputs.name: Service configuration
inputs.description: Required credentials and the connection to the external data store.

outputs.primary: A continuously available BWS4 reachable securely by visitors, with embedding and projection ready from startup.
outputs.schema_notes: Behaviour-preserving: no example app, usage cap or visitor-facing message changes. The previous host is fully retired. The instance has 4 GB of guaranteed memory.

success_criteria: The public address serves the client and services over a valid certificate.
The first visit after quiet periods has no cold-start delay.
Memory stays comfortably within the available allowance with the embedding model loaded.
Every example app, cap and message behaves as before the move.
Nothing remains live at the previous host.

failure_modes.mode: Certificate expires or is misconfigured
failure_modes.mitigation: Renew automatically and monitor expiry so visitors never see a security warning.

failure_modes.mode: Instance stops or becomes unreachable
failure_modes.mitigation: Recover automatically on failure and monitor availability.

failure_modes.mode: Memory pressure from the embedding model
failure_modes.mitigation: Monitor memory use against the allowance and alert before exhaustion.

failure_modes.mode: Behavioural drift from the previous host
failure_modes.mitigation: Compare example app behaviour, caps and messages before and after the move.

features.name: Router_Example_App
features.purpose: Illustrates routing: one cheap classification call chooses among four existing paths (deterministic evaluator, single call, RAG retrieval, search plus generation), after which code dispatches and the router steps aside. The app shows the decision, the answer, the cost against a no-router baseline, and measured agreement history.

invocation.trigger: The visitor picks one of six curated requests or types their own and runs it; after a mismatched preset run, the visitor may request one comparison re-run through the expected route.

inputs.name: Request
inputs.description: A preset (each with an expected route and one-line reason, no stored answer) or free text.

inputs.name: Route descriptions
inputs.description: One line per route, shown exactly as the router received them. The deterministic line is generated from the same table the evaluator checks; the RAG line carries the subject list derived at startup from the indexed documents.

inputs.name: Outcome and latency history
inputs.description: Recorded per-preset agreed, disagreed and declined counts and search-route timings from all visitors, which persist across service interruptions.

outputs.primary: A decision card (chosen route, one-line rationale, all four scores, and agreement status for presets), the dispatched path's answer labelled with its path, a cost strip against the no-router baseline, and per-preset agreement history.
outputs.format: Decision card, answer panel in the matching app's layout, cost comparison, history table
outputs.schema_notes: Router returns four scores plus a structured expression if the deterministic route scores highest. Scores are the model's uncalibrated self-report, and the measured agreement rate is the one calibrated number. A fixed margin in code triggers a low-confidence path that dispatches to the cheaper of the top two routes in the fixed cost order (deterministic, single call, RAG, search plus generation). Preset runs state 'agreed', 'misrouted' or 'declined'. The cost strip separates router overhead and always labels baseline time 'typical', showing counts only until at least five observations exist.

success_criteria: Every run ends as either a routed answer with its decision card and cost strip, or a low-confidence card naming the two routes it was torn between.
Deterministic calculations never run model-produced text; an expression the evaluator cannot compute is dispatched to single call and the card says so plainly as the router's own misroute.
If a low-confidence tie lands on deterministic and the evaluator rejects it, the other candidate route is used and the card says the evaluator could not compute it.
Each run costs at most 2 model-call units (1 on the deterministic route); 2 are reserved before the router runs and the second is released once the evaluator accepts.

A comparison re-run is offered only when the dispatched route differs from the expected route for a preset, does not run the router again, shows router overhead as zero, counts as one of the 5 visit runs, and feeds no history.
Free-text runs and re-runs feed no agreement cell, and a tie-break landing on the expected route earns no credit.
History cells show counts only until they have at least five observations.
A runs-remaining indicator is shown, and when exhausted the input and run controls are disabled with a message distinguishing the 5-run limit from the shared cap.

If route descriptions are not ready, the page shows 'temporarily unavailable' with a retry action, no run starts and no usage is reserved; a successful retry restores normal operation without restarting the service, while a failed retry keeps the message. Other apps are unaffected.

failure_modes.mode: Router picks the wrong route
failure_modes.mitigation: Show it candidly as 'misrouted', record it in the agreement history, and offer the comparison re-run for presets.

failure_modes.mode: Router returns an unusable or missing decision
failure_modes.mitigation: Treat it as 'declined' for presets and apply the low-confidence path.

failure_modes.mode: Expression is rejected by the evaluator
failure_modes.mitigation: Dispatch to the fallback route with the held units and state the correction on the card.

failure_modes.mode: Too little latency history for the baseline
failure_modes.mitigation: Show counts only with a note until enough search-route runs exist, never a made-up figure.

failure_modes.mode: Shared cap too close to complete a run
failure_modes.mitigation: Refuse before starting so no run begins and nothing is spent.

features.name: Codebase_Quality_And_Config_Cleanup
features.purpose: A behaviour-preserving cleanup that brings the whole codebase under full lint and type checking, makes the required credentials truly required, removes stale references to the retired host, and documents previously unrecorded edits.

invocation.trigger: Maintainers run this one-time cleanup before the next release; the checks then run in the normal quality gate.

inputs.name: Existing codebase
inputs.description: All source, tests, docs and configuration, including older modules currently excluded from checks.

inputs.name: Unrecorded edits
inputs.description: Site metadata, the shared generation service, project documentation, assistant settings, project configuration and ReAct frontend test changes awaiting review.

outputs.primary: A fully checked, consistently formatted codebase with no exclusions, updated documentation, and a written list of reviewed edits and any items flagged for the owner's decision.
outputs.format: Updated files plus a review note
outputs.schema_notes: No visible behaviour change except that startup now fails when either required credential is missing. Chained Calls 'critique_failed' behaviour and the Router route-id contract are unchanged. Anything that looks unintended is flagged, not silently reverted.

success_criteria: No lint or type-check exclusions remain and all findings are fixed.
Example app behaviour, routes, response shapes, usage caps and visitor messages are unchanged.
Startup fails clearly when either required credential is missing, with no placeholders or opt-out; tests require real credentials and the live smoke run stays opt-in.
No mention of the retired host remains in code, docs, configuration or release files, and the startup description matches the always-on instance.
Each unrecorded edit is documented as kept or flagged for the owner.
A one-time check confirms the Router code and tests are covered by the checks.
A failure while preparing route descriptions is logged, startup still succeeds, and the Router shows its unavailable state with a retry action until preparation succeeds.

failure_modes.mode: Fixing findings accidentally changes behaviour
failure_modes.mitigation: Run the full test suite and compare visible behaviour before and after.

failure_modes.mode: Stricter credential rule breaks test runs without credentials
failure_modes.mitigation: Document that real credentials are needed for every test run and communicate the change to maintainers.

failure_modes.mode: An unintended edit is kept without review
failure_modes.mitigation: Inspect each unrecorded edit and flag doubtful ones for the owner.

failure_modes.mode: A stale reference to the retired host is missed
failure_modes.mitigation: Sweep all code, docs, configuration and release files for it.

nfr_goals: The first visit loads without a cold-start delay because the embedding capability is ready at startup
The service refuses to start when a required credential is missing
Every example app stays within the shared hourly and daily usage limits so total spend is bounded
Per-run model-call counts are fixed and clearly stated in each app
Visitors are told clearly which limit (per-app visit limit or shared cap) stopped them
A failure in one example app or optional startup step does not affect the other apps
All traffic is served over a secure public address with a valid certificate
Routing and agreement history persists across service interruptions
Consistent layout and navigation across all example apps
